Clear the enemies and reach the boss!
Welcome back to reality, traveler. Or rather, what's left of it. I am Sarah, commander of the Meridian's Wardens. Breathe — we caught you mid-transfer. Your body is still deciding when it is.
...Where am I? {HomeEraName}? The sky... it tore apart, and something pulled.

An extraction beam. The ones who fired it call themselves the Unbound — a sect from my century that went to war over the right to touch the past, and is losing. Losing makes them desperate. Now they attack history itself: cracking open its pivotal moments and draining them, remaking time in their favor. You were a target. You are the one we reached in time.
Then we must stop them. But what of the soldiers I saw? They looked like my people, but... wrong. Their eyes glowed, their weapons hummed with light.

The Unbound's doing. Where their siphons deploy, they neural-link the local inhabitants and force them to defend the machines as 'Altered Mobs' — steam automatons overcharged with chronal energy, knights with energy shields. Alongside them you will face the Unbound's own infantry from the future. Seal the moment and the siphons die — the link breaks.

Time protects itself. When they tore your moment open, history armed the only anchor it had left — you. Everything your era is poured itself into its legend rather than let them take it. We call it Temporal Resonance.
Your combat resonance is calibrated. Now let's test your spatial awareness — you'll need every advantage to navigate the fractured timelines.
Calibration complete. The time portals are unlocked — return to the bridge and choose your first destination.
Florence... it should be beautiful. But there's machinery here that doesn't belong to this century.

Stay alert. The Severed have deployed a siphon in Da Vinci's workshop. The city guards have been neural-linked. They are armed with shock-pikes. Do not let their electrical discharges lock your movements.
My master paid for the maestro's war machines. These future men deliver them faster.
The siphon is shattered. The energy is dispersing.
Outstanding. With the siphon gone, the neural-link is broken. The Linked guards will wake with nothing but a headache, thinking it was a strange dream.
And the master of this workshop? Half-built wonders, ink still warm on the drafting table... and no Da Vinci. Where is he?
...I don't know. The record says he never left this room in 1503. Yet the era stands — as if history is holding its breath for him. Come home. I need to look at the other eras.

The bridge is yours, {HeroAddressName}. This ship is cut off from my own century, so what you see is what we have — the Chronal Repository will bank your dust, and the Holodeck can spar you against simulated foes.
When you are ready, the Temporal Portal is charged for your next destination. History is waiting.

LEVEL 2: THE SIEGE OF ORLÉANS — ORLÉANS 1429
Break through the English lines toward the siege works.
The barriers are down. Take the battlement.
Orléans, 1429. The English have the city ringed — and the Severed have given them shields no army of this age should have.

Watch the clock on your display. That's this moment's integrity — how much of it still holds. Every Extractor they've planted drains it faster. Break one and the bleeding slows. Nothing gives back what's already lost.
The French wait for a girl who isn't coming. Neither is their victory.
The shield towers are down and the link is broken. Look — they're charging.
Without her. Her banner, her army... and no Joan. Another one missing from her own moment.
Cross the fairgrounds and reach the Electricity Building
Rotate the conductive coils to route the beam into the receiver
The Court of Honor is open — press on!
Chicago, 1893. The World's Fair — the night a hundred thousand lamps were meant to prove alternating current safe.
The Severed have hung siphon coils across the fairgrounds. If they overload, the lights won't just fail — they'll burn the crowd.
Alternating current kills. Tonight, the whole world watches it prove me right.
The lamps are holding. The link's broken — the whole fair is lit.
Lit by Tesla's system — without Tesla. {MissingSoFar}, now him. This isn't chance, Commander.
...No. I don't think it is. Come home. I want a closer look at the shards.
Breach the Bastille and reach the inner courtyard
Caught in the beam! The dampener is draining your Ultimate — break the light
Blow the cell locks and free the prisoners ({0}/{1})
The prisoners have hauled the gate open — breach the inner courtyard
INNER COURTYARD BARRED — FREE THE PRISONERS
Paris, 14 July 1789. The city has come for the Bastille — and the Severed have fortified it with things no king ever owned.
Forcefields, searchlights, and dampening beams that drain your meter if they catch you. Stay out of the light.
This fortress has never fallen. With these gifts, it never will.
The Bastille has fallen — as it should. The link is broken.
They took a man who wasn't a legend, Commander. Desmoulins was a voice, not a king.
He isn't one I'd have guessed they'd want. The record has him here. It doesn't have him anywhere now.
Climb sternward before the flooding overtakes you
Reach the boat deck — the water is still rising
The harvest is broken. Return to the Time-Ship.
The Titanic, 15 April 1912. She's already struck the ice. The Severed have a siphon aboard, and they're drinking the whole night dry.
The water's rising room by room. You won't outrun it forever — keep moving.
{HeroAddressName}, their siphon is anchored at the stern rail — and something is standing guard over it.
Then it stands between me and the siphon.
Engage it and that deck will not stay dry. Keep to the gantries and finish it fast.
The one that got away. The hunters were meant to spare me the trouble.
...Come home. Their Overseer carried an encrypted key — it points somewhere off this world. I'll start on it.
Cross the moored fleet unseen and reach the storm-anchor ship
In the lantern light! A thunder-bomb volley lands in seconds — break line of sight
Cut the lantern signal lines to darken the fleet lanterns ({0}/{1})
Every lantern is dark and the boarding gate is open — reach the flagship deck
BOARDING GATE BARRED — CUT THE LANTERN SIGNAL LINES
Hakata Bay, 1281. The largest fleet the world has ever seen, anchored off Japan's coast — and the samurai are rowing out to it at night in open boats.
The Severed have moored storm-anchors among the ships to drink the typhoon that's coming. Stay out of the lanterns.
The wind will not save you this time. We have tamed the wind.
The anchors are gone. Listen — the wind's rising.
Wade the shifting dunes and find a way beneath the siege line
Find the hieroglyph seal — the order is carved somewhere in the tombs
Press the glyphs in the carved order ({0}/{1})
The vault is open — reach Cleopatra's chambers before the legion does
HIEROGLYPH SEAL — PRESS THE GLYPHS IN THE CARVED ORDER
CARVED ORDER — SCARAB · IBIS · FALCON · JACKAL
Alexandria, 30 BC. Octavian's legions are at the gates, and the Severed have wired the palace itself.
There are locks beneath the palace older than Rome — hieroglyph seals. Read them before you force them.
The queen has gone to the gods. I speak for them now.
The Jackal Priest is beaten, and the guards breathe freely again... but these are the queen's own chambers. Where is Cleopatra?
Nowhere. Her guards defended an empty throne with future fire. The era holds its breath — like {MissingPlaces}. Every giant, missing from their own moment.
Taken. The way they took the captain.
...Or torn loose, the way you nearly were. That is my hope. The Observation Deck is scanning the shards. We will find them.
The siphon is shattered. The sand is just sand again.
Confirmed. The link is down across the whole delta. Octavian's legion and the palace guard both come back to themselves, and the siege ends the way history wrote it — not one hour worse.
The vault is sealed and the delta is quiet. It is the emptiest victory I have carried out of an era yet.
Act II runs harder than Act I, {HeroAddressName}, and every anchor ahead is bigger than one palace. Whatever you reclaimed in there is yours now — you are going to need all of it.
Then stop warning me and take me home, Commander. There is another one waiting.
Get the citizens out before Vesuvius buries the city
Balance the winch — both stone pans must carry the same load
The road east is open. Run.
The flow caught you — keep moving east!
Reach the thermal anchor on the caldera rim
The harvest is broken. Return to the Time-Ship.
ROAD BURIED — HAUL THE ROCKFALL CLEAR
Pompeii, 79 AD. Vesuvius is already waking. The Severed have anchored their siphons at the caldera to drink the eruption.
The eruption itself — can we stop it?
No. The mountain does what it did. We make sure the people who got out, get out.
The mountain gives more than any city ever could. Stand aside, or burn with it.
The anchors are down. The mountain is its own again.
Pliny's galleys waited for a man who never came. An admiral, a captain, a voice in a crowd... They're not only taking legends.
The Navy is shelling the harbour. Get to the moorings.
Cross the channel and board the burning flagship.
The targeting grid is dead. Return to the Time-Ship.
Nassau, 1715. A pirate haven that governs itself by vote — and the Severed have moored their siphons in its harbor.
The crews have been linked. Ship to ship is the only road; mind the water.
Pirates, defending a machine they can't even see.
Every crew in this harbor sails under my flag now. Even the ones who don't know it.
The siphons are sunk, and the crews are waking — confused, and very angry.
Free again. For a few more years.
Until the King's pardon comes. Most of them take it. History's kinder to pirates than you'd think.
Cross the yard and get up onto the stage
Cross the stage — the boards shake before they drop
The galleries have you marked — move!
Swing the rigging up through the galleries to the tiring-house
The Globe, around 1601 — Hamlet's first performance. The Severed have hidden siphons in the galleries and under the stage.
The whole house has been linked, audience and company both. Keep moving — a bored crowd starts throwing things.
Then I'd best give them a show.
Every king in this play dies. Not this one.
The link's broken. They're finishing the play — the last act, and a quiet house.
Without the man who wrote it. How many does that make, Commander?
LEVEL 11: THE GETTYSBURG BATTLEFIELD — PENNSYLVANIA, JULY 1863
Advance east across the battlefield — use the fences and sandbags for cover.
Both arrays are down. The Union line has the breastwork — follow it into the railcut.
CONFEDERATE BREASTWORK — BREAK THE SHIELDING ARRAYS
Gettysburg, July 1863. Three days that turned a war — and the Severed have planted siphons all across the field.
Their Linked batteries have laser artillery and shielding arrays. Break the arrays and the Union lines can move.
Range the one who glows. Fire!
The arrays are down. Listen — the field's gone quiet.
No. But it's theirs. Come home — the key from the Titanic is almost cracked.
Cross the mare and reach the Severed outpost
Mind the vacuum vents — the low route is the loud route
Ride the spire lift and take the highline over the curtain wall
The broadcast is clean. Return to the Time-Ship.
The key's cracked. It was never pointing at an era — it was pointing at a relay. On the Moon. July 1969.
The Severed have built an outpost beside the landing site. They're drinking the moment the whole world looked up.
To think humanity would walk among the stars... and yet, the Severed have built a fortress of metal here.

Their last siphon nexus. Break it, and their roads through the rifts begin to close. And my trace is nearly done — every drained era, every stolen scrap of resonance... it has all been flowing somewhere. Get me past its guardian and this siphon will show me where.
The Overseer falls. With the nexus undefended, Sarah's trace completes.

...Coordinates. A fortress in the space between timelines. And inside it — resonance signatures. Alive. It's them. {CaptiveName1}. {CaptiveName2}. The others we lost. They were never adrift. The Severed have had them since the first strike — and their resonance is draining.
Then the eras were never the whole of it. Whatever they are building with the stolen years, it ends now. Set the portal, Commander.
You're a long way from your moment, little legend.
The relay is scrap. The broadcast is going out clean.

Confirmed. Every set on Earth is watching the real thing. The moment is sealed and every siphon on the outpost died with it — the Linked crew are coming back to themselves, and nobody down there will remember having been anything else.
I have never felt it this strong, Sarah. Everything I pulled off their machines up here is still in my hands.
Hold on to it. Where we are going next, you will need every scrap of it.
Then Act Two ends here. Take me through their front door, Commander.
Cross the rift and find the far corridor
Ride the loose era fragments — the shelf below is pooled with stalled time
The corridor is open. Return to the Time-Ship.

There is no ground here. There is no here here — only pieces. That is the flag from Tranquility Base, and that is a Bastille door, and they are falling past each other without either of them falling down.

You are between dimensions, {HeroAddressName}. The trace we pulled off the Overseer runs straight through it — the Unbound cut a corridor from their own century back through every fracture they ever made, and this is the spoil heap. Head east. The far side opens on the fortress.
Then I walk east on Orléans stone and Titanic decking. Tell me the moment the gravity is about to turn over.
You are the one that got away. They modelled you a thousand times to find out how — and I am the model that kept getting up.
Then you know exactly how I fight. So do I. Come on.
It went down the way I would have gone down. Same guard, same tell, same half-second too late. I have never had to watch myself lose before.

The corridor is holding. There was no siphon in here to shatter — the rift stopped tearing the moment that thing stopped drawing on it. And nothing living was ever caught in the Void, so there is nobody down there to send home. For once I have no casualty list to read you.
It fought like me, Sarah. Every guard, every tell. Somebody has been studying me long enough to build that.

Long enough to build it a thousand times over, by the look of this corridor. They are not improvising, and they have not been improvising since the first strike. The far end of this is their front door, and it is standing open.
Then let it be me who walks through it. Take me to the Bastion, Commander.
Time the perimeter lattice and breach the outer rampart
Ride the containment pockets across the Extraction Hall
Run the Forge spine to the core
The intake is dead. The Forge is firing — ride the channel.
There is no sky here. No ground either — just the fortress, hanging in the space between one century and the next.

That is the Bastion, {HeroAddressName}. Not a stolen era: the place they built outside all of them, and the room every siphon in history reported back to. It was made to keep people out, so the perimeter will be honest about it — security lattices on a fixed cycle, and anti-gravity containment fields they use to shift cargo. Read a lattice before you walk it. And mind the pockets: they will lift you a great deal further than you expect.
Then let us walk into the one place they never rehearsed losing.
You are a rounding error that learned to knock. I have catalogued every version of this conversation, and in the ones that matter you were filed a long time ago.
You have catalogued an awful lot of people who never got to answer you. I am the answer.
The intake is dark. Every siphon line in the Bastion went slack at once.

Confirmed — and the cradles are still holding. I want you to hear that part: we could not cut one of them loose, and the engine at the core is still charged. They come home when it dies, and not one minute before.
Then it dies today. The whole hall pulled at me on the way out, Sarah, and I am still carrying every scrap I took back off them.
Good, because there is exactly one route left and it is theirs. The Forge is firing, and the channel it opens only exists while it fires. We ride it in.
Then put me in the channel, Commander. One jump left, and nothing after it.
Ride the firing channel down to the Meridian Founding
Climb the founding terraces and force a way east
RUN — the channel is closing behind you
Clear the guard at the anchor seat
Seal the timeline at the half-seated Prime Anchor
The Prime Anchor is shattered. Every thread goes home.
Press Interact to seal the timeline
This is no era I can read. There is a city being founded down there, under a sky that has not decided what century it is.

The founding day of the Meridian, {HeroAddressName} — everything my order ever was starts this morning. The Forge fired at it, and the channel you rode in on is the shot. The First Unbound is already at the seat with the Prime Anchor half in.
Then we finish it where they started it.
The seat is through that door. Everything you have taken back since Florence is riding in you right now, and it is the one weight their anchor was never built to out-hold.
Standing over the stone with three phases of Unbound doctrine and a war it refuses to have lost. This is the last door, {HeroAddressName}. There is nothing after this one.

You are a footnote that learned to walk. I have unwritten empires, languages, entire centuries of a species that never noticed the subtraction. This morning I unwrite the order that beat me — and then I come back for the line in the ledger with your name on it.
You have been paying for me with other people's centuries since the first day. I am here to close the account.

It is down — and the Anchor is exposed, half in and still holding. That is it, {HeroAddressName}. Walk to the stone and seal it. Everything you have carried since the workshop goes into that one press.
Every era. All the way back.
It's shattering! The Forge is drinking its own backlash — the cradles are opening! The resonance — all of it — it's going home!

Threads of light arc out of the collapsing Prime Anchor and across every era. In Renaissance Florence, in Roman Pompeii, on the fields of Gettysburg, the fracture scars heal and the people lost to the extraction step back into their streets. {CaptiveName1} wakes in their own moment, then {CaptiveName2} — and every other legend, and the hundreds behind them, dissolves into golden light and reappears each in their own moment.
The resonance... it was never mine. It was history's — held in trust. Take it back.

The timelines are sealed. The war is over — and the future you saved is the one you're standing in. Thank you, {HeroAddressName}. You will wake where they tried to take you from. You will remember the Time-Ship, the battle, and the friends you fought beside... but the rifts are closed forever. You are going home.
History... is ours to write now.
{HeroName} disappears — last of all the legends. The Founding's sky clears, and the Meridian's first day proceeds, untouched.

key: # Level 0: the First Strike adds a seventh line
en: and the nexus question is per-hero.

We couldn't stop the beam. We could hold it — a few seconds. That was enough for the fire to finish catching. You are the one they fired on and did not get. Now — we calibrate it. Step up to the bay console.
...Where am I? My study. Princeton — the blackboard was an arm's length away. The sky tore apart over the elms, and something pulled.
...Where am I? The vanguard field before Orléans. I had the banner in my hands. The sky tore apart, and something pulled.
...Where am I? My workshop. Florence — the ornithopter was still on the bench. The sky tore apart, and something pulled.
...Where am I? The field at Gettysburg. I had not finished the address. The sky tore apart, and something pulled.
...Where am I? My own chambers. Alexandria — the envoys were still waiting. The sky tore apart above the palace, and something pulled.
...Where am I? The laboratory. The coil was still singing. The sky tore apart, and something pulled.
...Where am I? The Globe. The fifth act unwritten on the table. The sky tore apart above the yard, and something pulled.
...Where am I? Vienna — mid-concerto, the hall holding its breath. The sky tore apart, and something pulled.
...Where am I? The Tidewater. The river path home. The sky tore apart, and something pulled.

Joan! The line needs you at the banner.
Mr. Tesla! Help us bring the lights back.

key: # N03 hero-variant replacements for the six absence reports.

en: My own workshop, turned into their siphon. They didn't care what it was — only what it held.
Then Florence has its master back. But the record says you are not the only giant pulled from their moment. Come home. I need to look at the other eras.
They charged at my banner. I should have been here to raise it.
You're here now. But Florence's master is still missing — and I don't think he's the only one.
My lamps. My current. And I was not here to throw the switch.
You threw it now. But Florence and Orléans lost their legends too. That's a pattern, not chance.
The Jackal Priest is beaten, and my guards breathe freely again. They held these chambers against a throne they had been told was empty.
They did — and every other era on my board still holds its breath, like {MissingPlaces}. Every giant, missing from their own moment. You are the only one of them standing in theirs.
They're playing it through to the end. I'd almost forgotten how it ends.
Then come home and remember. There are still others missing.
I sent them into this field. I should have been at the telegraph when it ended.
You're here now. The others still aren't. Come home — the key from the Titanic is almost cracked.

key: # N04 captive spoken names (Leonardo's differs from his roster display name).

en: By every saint and star... the hall goes on beyond sight. The legends — wired into the machines like lamps into a chandelier. And behind them... hundreds more.

Extraction Cradles. This is where every stolen era went — they were never spending the energy, they were banking it. All of it feeds that engine at the core. Do NOT touch the cradles! Sever a thread while the machine is charged and the machine keeps them — forever. The only way to free them is to kill it.

The Warden is half right. It is called the Anchor Forge, little legend, and it was calibrated for all of you. The others we caged before their fire could catch. Yours caught — history flinched, and hid itself inside you. Every era we burned since, we burned to fill the hole you left. The deficit in my ledger carries your name. Lie down in a cradle — and history keeps the rest.
My legacy is not yours to spend. I will break your Forge — and every thread in this hall goes home.

key: # N05 scarred-ending variant of the final narration beat (selection logic is A3b's).

en: {HeroName} disappears — last of all the legends. The Founding's sky clears, but the plaza keeps the Prime Anchor's scar: a long cold seam across the stone that the Meridian will never quite finish explaining.

key: # Per-act hub refresh: Sarah and Medic Okafor on the Observation Deck.

en: The eras I send you into keep coming back with a hole in them, {HeroAddressName} — the one person each moment was built around, gone. I have stopped calling that a coincidence on the log.
Whatever you took back off their machines out there stays with you. Carry it into the next one.
Every era you seal cuts one more of their roads, and you come back off each one heavier than you went in. That is the only arithmetic in this war that runs our way.
The Observation Deck is still sweeping the shards for the others. Nothing yet. The portal is charged when you are.
No more eras, {HeroAddressName}. From here it is their ground, their corridor and their fortress, and there is no way back to this deck between them.
Everything history handed you is still in your hands. Take all of it through that portal.
Medic Okafor. Sit, please — I read everyone who comes through that portal, before and after. Your resonance baseline is up eleven points since Florence.
That is not what the Commander expected, and I would rather she were wrong in this direction. Go carefully.
Up again. Whatever you are pulling out of their siphons is not passing through you, {HeroAddressName} — it is staying.
I have also finished the era sweep the Commander asked for. Vienna, 1787. No Mozart. I have stopped being surprised and started keeping a list.
The readings are off my scale now. I have nothing to compare you to except the day we pulled you off that beam.
Come back and let me take one more. That is all I am asking of you.

The field closed. The cradle finished what it started, and no rift came.

It nearly had you. Your anchor held — get up.
Pick a legend to train with. Every kit here is the normalized Fighter loadout - no Resonance, no campaign progress, nothing to lose.
Six short lessons in the universal verbs. Each one is pass or fail, and you can retry as often as you like.
Stand your ground and hold Block. Let two of the dummy's string break on your shield.
That is the shield doing its job - and from the second hit of a string you can escape the stun straight back into it.
You ate the whole string. Block works only on the ground, and only while you hold it.
Let the dummy launch you, then hold Block as you hit the floor to tech the landing.
Clean tech. A teched landing is invulnerable and instant - it is how you refuse the follow-up.
You landed flat. Hold Block through the landing itself, not at the moment of the launch.
Take the dummy's finisher and hold a direction during the hit freeze. That is Directional Influence.
You steered it. DI cannot cancel a launch, but it decides where the launch leaves you.
You went wherever they sent you. Hold a direction during the freeze, before the launch resolves.
The dummy is holding Block and will not drop it. Walk in, grab it, and throw.
Attack loses to block, block loses to grab, grab loses to attack. You just closed the triangle.
No throw landed. A grab is Block plus Attack, on the ground, inside jab range.
Charge Influence to 30 by attacking the training bag.
Now swing, and press Block plus Roll during the recovery - Echo Step folds you back to where you stood.
That is a swing you no longer have to finish standing still. It costs 30 Influence and will not answer again immediately.
No step fired. It answers only out of your own swing's recovery frames, and only with 30 Influence banked.
Take the dummy's hit, then land one of your own before the echo drains away.
Reclaimed. Damage taken leaves an echo for a moment; hitting back turns it straight back into health.
The echo drained away. Answer faster - a reclaim lands only while the echo is still on the bar.
Siphon tether: drains Influence inside the ring. Block it, break line of sight, or leave the circle.

key: # M16 Resonance Hold held-Interact channel and N01 sealing anchor (W8 parent).

en: Hold Interact to seal the severed conduit
Hold Interact to shut the intake valve
Hold Interact to release the anchor pylon
Seal the timeline at the anchor
Florence — my Florence. And someone has been building with my designs.
Maestro. His Excellency still wants his engineer.
I drew Cesare maps and bridges — not this. I left his service. Tell him so.
The Maid planted her banner and told us to wait for her word. Then she was gone. The men won't charge without her.
Then the current needs someone to steer it.
Those mirror coils can bend the beams away from the crowds. Read the room before you run it.
Mr. Tesla built this system — only he can tune it. He was here last night checking the dynamos. This morning his coat was still on the hook, and he was gone.
Break their locks and they'll fight beside you. It's their revolution — let them have it.
Desmoulins was meant to lead us — he stood on a table and called all Paris to arms! Now no one can find him. Who's to tell us what we came for?
Too many. Stay on the siphon.
The captain — they took him. The way they tried to take me.
...An extraction beam, on a man with no power to fight it. I don't know why him.
There are still people below decks. If we seal this, the ship goes down with them.

I know. The Severed don't care who lives or dies tonight — they only want the power bleeding out of it. Leave their siphon running and this night never ends, and everything that came after it starts to come apart.

Not the ship. Not the ones history lost. But every soul who reached a lifeboat that night will reach one again — because you closed it. That's what restoring time means. Some nights, it's the hardest thing we do.
The lifeboats row clear as the lights go out.
The admiral was to lead the galleys in himself. We waited on the tide — he never came aboard.
They'd defend it with their lives. That's what the link does.
Another hunter. It isn't guarding the siphons — it's looking for you.
We hold the throne for her. She told us she would return by nightfall. That was three nights ago.
A storm that saves a nation.
It still comes. It always comes. We just make sure it arrives whole.
It's trying to finish what the beam started — pull away!
That pull... it was the beam. The same as the night you found me.
I know. I saw it on the readings. Keep moving.
Master Shakespeare was to bring the last act this morning. The prompt-book stops mid-scene, and he's nowhere.
The President's orders stopped coming. No word from Washington in days — the telegraph just hums.
Six hundred million people. Don't give them anything to see.
I saw the other beams that hour. I saw who was inside them — and I could not reach one of them. I told myself they were gone, and I let you believe you were the only one. I was wrong to. I'm sorry.
